Active Lives Adults — Somerset 2024/25

Annual data through 2024/25. Generated 2026-09-22.

Internal validation draft. These are weighted descriptive percentages, not verified replicas of Sport England tables. Confidence intervals and significance claims are intentionally absent pending verification of the survey-design method. Unapproved indicator weights are omitted and listed below. Check the Somerset geography across years before circulation.

Percentages use valid coded responses with a positive finite indicator weight. Counts are rounded only after calculation. Cells below 8 and complementary cells are suppressed; displayed counts are rounded to 5. These disclosure settings carry forward the old project convention and require confirmation against the prescribed guidance. A blank is never interpreted as zero participation.

2016/17;2017/18;2018/19;2019/20;2020/21: Readiness was grouped as strongly agree versus other valid responses. Negative missing codes and any code 0 labelled 'Not asked' were excluded. Where respondents were skipped because they were already sufficiently active, estimates describe valid respondents to the question, not all adults. Comparisons with years using different routing require caution. adult_readiness_processing, Grouping and eligible respondents.

2016/17: Readiness was asked below the questionnaire-calculated 150-minute weekly activity threshold. Percentages describe eligible respondents with valid answers, not all adults. Routing exclusions and other missing responses are excluded. These estimates use wt_final_online; comparisons with years using broader question eligibility are not like-for-like. adult_2016_online_questionnaire, Readiness routing and analysis denominator.

2017/18: Readiness was asked below the questionnaire-calculated 150-minute weekly activity threshold. Percentages describe eligible respondents with valid answers, not all adults. Routing exclusions and other missing responses are excluded. These estimates use wt_final_online; comparisons with years using broader question eligibility are not like-for-like. adult_2017_online_questionnaire, Readiness routing and analysis denominator.

2017/18: Report-author-approved analytical decision: retain 20 valid responses labelled PAPER, all with positive supplied online weights. The reason for the mode discrepancy is unresolved; retention is not a confirmed Sport England instruction. adult_2026_review_decisions, Mode discrepancy.

2018/19: 2018/19 loneliness uses wt_final_C, the online group 2 weight, as specified in the Year 4 User Guide, Table 6. Percentages exclude routing exclusions and other missing responses. adult_2018, Weighting, Table 6; supplied-file response coverage.

2019/20: 2019/20 loneliness uses wt_final_AB: postal and online group 1. Online group 2 responses are excluded because question-order effects made them incomparable, as explained in the technical report. Missing responses and non-positive or missing weights are excluded. adult_2019_technical_loneliness, Printed page 6, footnote 6 (PDF page 15).

How happy did you feel yesterday (grouped)

2017/18: For 2017/18, happiness categories were reconstructed from the original 0–10 score using the supplied category definitions: 0–4 low, 5–6 medium, 7–8 high and 9–10 very high. Cross-tabulation showed that the supplied grouped variable did not consistently follow these boundaries. Negative missing codes were excluded. This is an analyst correction, not a revised data release. adult_2017_happiness_regrouping, Reconstruction of happiness categories.

How satisfied with life nowadays (grouped)

2017/18: Life satisfaction categories for 2017/18 were reconstructed from the original 0–10 score using the supplied definitions: 0–4 low, 5–6 medium, 7–8 high and 9–10 very high. Cross-tabulation showed that the supplied grouped variable did not consistently follow these boundaries. Negative missing codes were excluded. This is an analyst correction, not a revised data release. adult_2017_lifesat_regrouping, Reconstruction of wellbeing categories.

2017/18: Worthwhile categories for 2017/18 were reconstructed from the original 0–10 score using the supplied definitions: 0–4 low, 5–6 medium, 7–8 high and 9–10 very high. Cross-tabulation showed that the supplied grouped variable did not consistently follow these boundaries. Negative missing codes were excluded. This is an analyst correction, not a revised data release. adult_2017_worthw_regrouping, Reconstruction of wellbeing categories.

Readiness for activity: Ability (REBASED & GROUPED)

2016/17;2017/18;2018/19;2019/20;2020/21: Readiness was grouped as strongly agree versus other valid responses. Negative missing codes and any code 0 labelled 'Not asked' were excluded. Where respondents were skipped because they were already sufficiently active, estimates describe valid respondents to the question, not all adults. Comparisons with years using different routing require caution. adult_readiness_processing, Grouping and eligible respondents.

2016/17: Readiness was asked below the questionnaire-calculated 150-minute weekly activity threshold. Percentages describe eligible respondents with valid answers, not all adults. Routing exclusions and other missing responses are excluded. These estimates use wt_final_online; comparisons with years using broader question eligibility are not like-for-like. adult_2016_online_questionnaire, Readiness routing and analysis denominator.

2017/18: Readiness was asked below the questionnaire-calculated 150-minute weekly activity threshold. Percentages describe eligible respondents with valid answers, not all adults. Routing exclusions and other missing responses are excluded. These estimates use wt_final_online; comparisons with years using broader question eligibility are not like-for-like. adult_2017_online_questionnaire, Readiness routing and analysis denominator.

2017/18: Report-author-approved analytical decision: retain 20 valid responses labelled PAPER, all with positive supplied online weights. The reason for the mode discrepancy is unresolved; retention is not a confirmed Sport England instruction. adult_2026_review_decisions, Mode discrepancy.

Motivation for sport/exercise: I feel that doing sport/exercise is pointless (REBASED & GROUPED)

2016/17;2017/18;2018/19;2019/20;2020/21;2021/22;2022/23: Percentages describe strong agreement among eligible respondents with valid answers to item E, not among all adults. The reviewed questionnaires ask E only after neutral/disagree/strongly disagree responses to all preceding motivation items A-D. Respondents not asked and other missing responses are excluded, not counted as disagreeing. Analysis uses wt_final_online. This conditional denominator is the analytical approach adopted for this report. adult_2026_review_decisions, Conditional motivation denominator.

2016/17: The questionnaire routes item E on both the sport and exercise branches to respondents selecting response 3, 4 or 5 on each of A-D. adult_2016_online_questionnaire, Motivation routing.

2017/18: The questionnaire routes item E on both the sport and exercise branches to respondents selecting response 3, 4 or 5 on each of A-D. adult_2017_online_questionnaire, Motivation routing.

2017/18: Analytical decision: retain eight valid PAPER-labelled responses with positive supplied online weights, following the report-author-approved approach to the readiness mode discrepancy. Their origin remains unresolved. adult_2026_review_decisions, Mode discrepancy.

How often do you feel lonely?

2020/21: 2020/21 loneliness estimates are temporarily omitted. The Year 6 User Guide specifies wt_lone, but that weight was not found in the directly shared dataset. The appropriate weight for this file remains unresolved. adult_2020, Weighting, Table 5; supplied-file weight inventory.

2018/19: 2018/19 loneliness uses wt_final_C, the online group 2 weight, as specified in the Year 4 User Guide, Table 6. All 52,502 valid responses in the supplied file are online and have positive values for this weight. Percentages exclude routing exclusions and other missing responses. adult_2018, Weighting, Table 6; supplied-file response coverage.

2019/20: 2019/20 loneliness uses wt_final_AB: postal and online group 1. Online group 2 responses are excluded because question-order effects made them incomparable, as explained in the technical report. Missing responses and non-positive or missing weights are excluded. adult_2019_technical_loneliness, Printed page 6, footnote 6 (PDF page 15).

Historical notes and data gaps

all — weights: Adult weights depend on the question and questionnaire group. Rows marked review in config/variables.csv are not analysed until their weight is checked; the imported data remain available. 9598_active_lives_survey_year_9_data_user_guide_v3_final.pdf, Weighting, Table 5; consult each annual guide.

2016/17 — volany: For 2016/17, Volint_ANY contains unlabelled valid codes 0 and 1. These were interpreted as No and Yes respectively, consistent with the labelled 2017/18 and 2018/19 files. This is an analyst assumption; the supplied 2016/17 documentation does not confirm these meanings. Negative missing/routing codes were excluded from the denominator. Analyst coding decision: 2016/17 volunteering, Analyst assumption approved for this report.

2016/17;2017/18;2018/19;2019/20;2020/21 — readyab1_pop_gr2: Readiness was grouped as strongly agree versus other valid responses. Negative missing codes and any code 0 labelled 'Not asked' were excluded. Where respondents were skipped because they were already sufficiently active, estimates describe valid respondents to the question, not all adults. Comparisons with years using different routing require caution. Analyst processing note: readiness, Grouping and eligible respondents.

2016/17;2017/18;2018/19 — readyop1_pop_gr2: Readiness was grouped as strongly agree versus other valid responses. Negative missing codes and any code 0 labelled 'Not asked' were excluded. Where respondents were skipped because they were already sufficiently active, estimates describe valid respondents to the question, not all adults. Comparisons with years using different routing require caution. Analyst processing note: readiness, Grouping and eligible respondents.

2017/18 — wellb_anxious_gr: For 2017/18, anxiety categories were reconstructed from the original 0–10 score using the supplied category definitions: 0–1 very low, 2–3 low, 4–5 medium and 6–10 very high. Cross-tabulation showed that the supplied grouped variable did not consistently follow these boundaries. Negative missing codes were excluded. This is an analyst correction, not a revised data release. Analyst processing note: 2017/18 anxiety, Reconstruction of anxiety categories.

2017/18 — wellb_happy_gr: For 2017/18, happiness categories were reconstructed from the original 0–10 score using the supplied category definitions: 0–4 low, 5–6 medium, 7–8 high and 9–10 very high. Cross-tabulation showed that the supplied grouped variable did not consistently follow these boundaries. Negative missing codes were excluded. This is an analyst correction, not a revised data release. Analyst processing note: 2017/18 happiness, Reconstruction of happiness categories.

2017/18 — wellb_lifesat_gr: Life satisfaction categories for 2017/18 were reconstructed from the original 0–10 score using the supplied definitions: 0–4 low, 5–6 medium, 7–8 high and 9–10 very high. Cross-tabulation showed that the supplied grouped variable did not consistently follow these boundaries. Negative missing codes were excluded. This is an analyst correction, not a revised data release. Analyst processing note: 2017/18 Life satisfaction, Reconstruction of wellbeing categories.

2017/18 — wellb_worthw_gr: Worthwhile categories for 2017/18 were reconstructed from the original 0–10 score using the supplied definitions: 0–4 low, 5–6 medium, 7–8 high and 9–10 very high. Cross-tabulation showed that the supplied grouped variable did not consistently follow these boundaries. Negative missing codes were excluded. This is an analyst correction, not a revised data release. Analyst processing note: 2017/18 Worthwhile, Reconstruction of wellbeing categories.

2016/17 — readyab1_pop_gr2: Readiness was asked below the questionnaire-calculated 150-minute weekly activity threshold. Percentages describe eligible respondents with valid answers, not all adults. Routing exclusions and other missing responses are excluded. These estimates use wt_final_online; comparisons with years using broader question eligibility are not like-for-like. 8391_active_lives_adult_online_questionnaire_scripting_internal_and_client.pdf, Readiness routing and analysis denominator.

2017/18 — readyab1_pop_gr2: Readiness was asked below the questionnaire-calculated 150-minute weekly activity threshold. Percentages describe eligible respondents with valid answers, not all adults. Routing exclusions and other missing responses are excluded. These estimates use wt_final_online; comparisons with years using broader question eligibility are not like-for-like. Active Lives Adult questionnaire (core), Year 3 FINAL, Readiness routing and analysis denominator.

2017/18 — readyab1_pop_gr2: Report-author-approved analytical decision: retain 20 valid responses labelled PAPER, all with positive supplied online weights. The reason for the mode discrepancy is unresolved; retention is not a confirmed Sport England instruction. Analyst review decisions, 13 September 2026, Mode discrepancy.

2016/17 — readyop1_pop_gr2: Readiness was asked below the questionnaire-calculated 150-minute weekly activity threshold. Percentages describe eligible respondents with valid answers, not all adults. Routing exclusions and other missing responses are excluded. These estimates use wt_final_online; comparisons with years using broader question eligibility are not like-for-like. 8391_active_lives_adult_online_questionnaire_scripting_internal_and_client.pdf, Readiness routing and analysis denominator.

2017/18 — readyop1_pop_gr2: Readiness was asked below the questionnaire-calculated 150-minute weekly activity threshold. Percentages describe eligible respondents with valid answers, not all adults. Routing exclusions and other missing responses are excluded. These estimates use wt_final_online; comparisons with years using broader question eligibility are not like-for-like. Active Lives Adult questionnaire (core), Year 3 FINAL, Readiness routing and analysis denominator.

2017/18 — readyop1_pop_gr2: Report-author-approved analytical decision: retain 20 valid responses labelled PAPER, all with positive supplied online weights. The reason for the mode discrepancy is unresolved; retention is not a confirmed Sport England instruction. Analyst review decisions, 13 September 2026, Mode discrepancy.

2016/17;2017/18;2018/19;2019/20;2020/21;2021/22;2022/23 — motive_pop_gr2: Percentages describe strong agreement among eligible respondents with valid answers to item E, not among all adults. The reviewed questionnaires ask E only after neutral/disagree/strongly disagree responses to all preceding motivation items A-D. Respondents not asked and other missing responses are excluded, not counted as disagreeing. Analysis uses wt_final_online. This conditional denominator is the analytical approach adopted for this report. Analyst review decisions, 13 September 2026, Conditional motivation denominator.

2016/17 — motive_pop_gr2: The questionnaire routes item E on both the sport and exercise branches to respondents selecting response 3, 4 or 5 on each of A-D. 8391_active_lives_adult_online_questionnaire_scripting_internal_and_client.pdf, Motivation routing.

2017/18 — motive_pop_gr2: The questionnaire routes item E on both the sport and exercise branches to respondents selecting response 3, 4 or 5 on each of A-D. Active Lives Adult questionnaire (core), Year 3 FINAL, Motivation routing.

2017/18 — motive_pop_gr2: Analytical decision: retain eight valid PAPER-labelled responses with positive supplied online weights, following the report-author-approved approach to the readiness mode discrepancy. Their origin remains unresolved. Analyst review decisions, 13 September 2026, Mode discrepancy.

2020/21 — lone: 2020/21 loneliness estimates are temporarily omitted. The Year 6 User Guide specifies wt_lone, but that weight was not found in the directly shared dataset. The appropriate weight for this file remains unresolved. 8993_active_lives_survey_full_year_6_data_user_guide_final.pdf, Weighting, Table 5; supplied-file weight inventory.

2018/19 — lone: 2018/19 loneliness uses wt_final_C, the online group 2 weight, as specified in the Year 4 User Guide, Table 6. All 52,502 valid responses in the supplied file are online and have positive values for this weight. Percentages exclude routing exclusions and other missing responses. 8652_active_lives_adult_data_user_guide_full_year_4_nov_18-19_final.pdf, Weighting, Table 6; supplied-file response coverage.

2019/20 — lone: 2019/20 loneliness uses wt_final_AB: postal and online group 1. Online group 2 responses are excluded because question-order effects made them incomparable, as explained in the technical report. Missing responses and non-positive or missing weights are excluded. Active Lives Survey 2019/2020 Year 5 Technical Report, Printed page 6, footnote 6 (PDF page 15).

adult_2016_volunteering_assumption: For 2016/17, Volint_ANY contains unlabelled valid codes 0 and 1. These were interpreted as No and Yes respectively, consistent with the labelled 2017/18 and 2018/19 files. This is an analyst assumption; the supplied 2016/17 documentation does not confirm these meanings. Negative missing/routing codes were excluded from the denominator.
